name: Terminal
author: Brett
description: Windows-style terminal: a Windows Terminal window with its own tab strip (rename, colour, drag to reorder, duplicate, move to a new window), a command toolbar and Windows keys. Claude Code tabs open on any connection (console container, VPS root, any container, axHub) through a connection picker; right-click a tab for its Connection manager. Claude Code profiles (model, permissions, flags, folder, first prompt, colour, default connection). Live settings: colour schemes, font, cursor, line height, padding, bell, scrollback, startup, tab width. Mouse mode, Mosh mode, copy/paste, phone key row, idle timeout and a session log. Settings → Plugins → Terminal. Persistent tabs: VPS and console tabs live in tmux sessions that survive reloads, sleep and restarts (Open in Moshi copies the attach command; closing detaches, Kill session ends one). Headless builds open their own tab with the agent, model, live cost and status, split into the session and its context chain. Sessions nav (left rail, collapsible): My sessions (Brett's own tmux / Claude Code sessions, mirrored read-only with Jump in; claude.ai chat and voice sessions as a live feed of their console_session_note lines and console MCP calls), Agents (headless builds with agent, model, live cost, status), Connections and Recent, live over a websocket.

items.title: List live sessions
items.description: Every session the Terminal's sessions nav lists: My sessions (Brett's tmux and Claude Code sessions, claude.ai chat feeds), Agents (headless builds with agent, model, cost, status), Connections and Recent.

items.title: Read a chat session's mirror feed
items.description: The lines a claude.ai chat or voice session posted (console_session_note) and the console MCP tools it called.

since.description: only lines after this epoch ms

items.title: Post a line into a session's mirror feed
items.description: Same as the MCP tool console_session_note.

items.title: Stop a session
items.description: End a tmux session for good (every device attached to it loses it).

items.title: Mirror a session in the open console
items.description: Open a read-only tab on a tmux session (or a chat's feed) in Brett's open Terminal. args: [name, where].

items.title: Jump into a session in the open console
items.description: Open a writable tab on a tmux session in Brett's open Terminal (a chat opens claude.ai). args: [name, where].

items.title: When a new session starts (Terminal)
items.description: What the Terminal does when a headless Claude session starts: nothing (no tab by itself), quiet (a tab in the background and a count on the Terminal toolbar icon; the default) or front (open it and bring the Terminal window to the front).

items.title: Set what the Terminal does when a new session starts
items.description: nothing | quiet (default: background tab + toolbar count, never pops the window) | front (bring the Terminal to the front).

items.skip: the sessions nav's live websocket, not a command (sessions-list is the same answer)

items.title: Open a Terminal tab on a target
items.description: Opens a terminal session on console, vps, container:<name>, build:<axf-name> (a headless build's session) or attach:<tmux>, and shows it as a tab in Brett's open console so he watches what is typed. Returns the session id the other drive commands take.

target.description: console | vps | container:<name> | build:<axf-name> | attach:<tmux session>

show.description: show the tab in the open console (default true)

items.output: the session (id, tmux, where, title) + shown

items.title: Type into a Terminal tab
items.description: Types the text visibly, character by character at the Terminal's typing speed (Settings → Plugins → Terminal → Typing speed, default 30 a second), then Enter, waits until the output goes quiet and returns what it printed and the screen.

id.description: session id from open-tab or tabs

enter.description: press Enter after the text (default true)

cps.description: characters a second for this call

items.title: Send keys to a Terminal tab
items.description: Sends named keys: enter, tab, shift-tab, esc, backspace, delete, up, down, left, right, home, end, pageup, pagedown, f1-f12, ctrl-<letter> (ctrl-c), alt-<key>, or single characters.

keys.description: one name, a space-separated string, or a list

items.title: Read a Terminal tab's screen
items.description: What the tab shows now, as plain text (its last lines; tmux tabs read the pane itself).

items.title: Close a Terminal tab
items.description: Closes the tab in the console and its session. A tab the API opened ends its own tmux session; kill: true ends any tab's tmux session too.

items.title: List Terminal tabs the API can type into
items.description: Every open terminal session (id, kind, title, tmux, where, writable) and the typing speed.
